about: The planned module map of TUIkit (buildtime/split2/refine/plan-refined.md, revision 4, after the owner's answers of 2026-10-07). Read by Tools/ModuleMap/modulemap.py; see README.md for every field. Since step A5 every module's files sit in Sources/<module>, so a file's directory is its module, and moving a file is a `git mv`. Paths are relative to Sources and start with the module's directory; declaration rules match '<path>::<name>', with '(ext)' after an extension's name. A module is renamed here, by renaming its directory (and the target, once carved), then `assign --write`.

modules.name: TUIkitStrings
modules.contents: Whole files needing no TUIkit module: the SF Symbols name table, the inline-Markdown parser, the format styles. Also the localization service, its string tables and keys, the module resource accessor (it holds the resources now) and storage diagnostics; it needs TUIkitCore (Lock) and compiles beside TUIkitView.

modules.name: TUIkitTerminalHost
modules.contents: Terminal facts as values: the host, its identity, quirks and capabilities, the process ancestry and clipboard locality behind them, hyperlink and clipboard support. View-free; needs TUIkitCore and compiles beside TUIkitView. The probes that fill these in stay in TUIkitApp.

modules.name: TUIkitFoundation
modules.contents: The default: everything no rule below claims, plus what two or more leaves or the substrate itself use.

modules.name: TUIkitChrome
modules.contents: The window chrome the run loop draws: the status bar view and its items, toolbars, notifications, tooltips and help, the window chrome host. The status bar STATE that focus and controls write stays in Base.

modules.name: TUIkitEffects
modules.contents: Transitions (.transition, AnyTransition, the built-in and custom transitions), content transitions, symbol effects, visual effects and scroll transitions.

modules.name: TUIkitBitmaps
modules.contents: The bitmap path of Image: Image(_:) from a file or URL, Image(_:bundle:), AsyncImage, decoding, resampling, orientation, templates, the render cache, the image-rendering options. Image itself and Image(systemName:) stay in Base. Base no longer depends on TUIkitImage.

modules.name: TUIkitMenus
modules.contents: Menu, ControlGroup, contextMenu, menuStyle and the concrete menu styles, the popup menu core, the option menu (SwiftUI: menus; its commands are TUIkitCommands', built on the scene). The dropdown renderer and popup machinery stay in Base: the screen-selection Copy menu and the popover use them. So do the inline menu's core and the menu column it lays out (_InlineMenuCore.swift, MenuColumnLayout.swift): the column calls Base's bordered and foregroundStyle, whose results name internal types, so only Base compiles it concrete (CONTRIBUTING.md, Crossing a module boundary; SPB5b diagnosis M1).

modules.name: TUIkitNumericControls
modules.contents: Slider, Stepper, Gauge, ProgressView: the controls that edit or show a number in a range; the track and indeterminate renderers they share, their styles and handlers (SwiftUI: getting numeric inputs, indicating a value).

modules.name: TUIkitTextInput
modules.contents: TextField, SecureField, TextEditor, their handlers, renderer, mouse handling, editing commands, undo, suggestions.

modules.name: TUIkitPickers
modules.contents: Picker, RadioButtonGroup (with its FormControlRow conformance), DatePicker, the picker and date-picker styles.

modules.name: TUIkitLists
modules.contents: List and _ListCore, ItemListHandler, list styles, row separators, insets and backgrounds, OutlineGroup, EditMode, row reorder, row shortcuts, selection context menus, the row memo Table shares.

modules.name: TUIkitGrid
modules.contents: Grid, GridRow, LazyVGrid, LazyHGrid, GridItem.

modules.name: TUIkitNavigation
modules.contents: NavigationStack, NavigationPath, NavigationLink, NavigationSplitView, HSplitView, VSplitView, Inspector, navigation destinations, crumbs.

modules.name: TUIkitPresentation
modules.contents: alert, confirmationDialog, Dialog, sheet, fullScreenCover and modal, dismissal confirmation, dialog suppression, presentation detents, sizing, background, interaction, traits.

modules.name: TUIkitForms
modules.contents: Form, LabeledContent, GroupBox, Card, Panel, their styles, FormButtonRow with Button's conformance (SwiftUI: view groupings).

modules.name: TUIkitSearch
modules.contents: searchable, search tokens and scopes, dismissSearch, search placement and toolbar behaviour.

modules.name: TUIkitTables
modules.contents: Table, columns, rows, builders, customization, outline rows, table styles, row drag and drop.

modules.name: TUIkitTabs
modules.contents: TabView, Tab, TabSection, TabContent with its builder and modifiers, tab styles.

modules.name: TUIkitColorPicker
modules.contents: ColorPicker, ColorPickerPanel and its swatches and grids, GradientEditorPanel and its stop chips (back from C9b's module on 2026-10-12), and the editor chrome and panel body the editors share. No TUIkitImage and no Pickers since C9b moved the curve editors out, so that an app with a ColorPicker links neither: the lower list keeps it so.

modules.name: TUIkitCurveEditors
modules.contents: The tone-curve and channel-curve editor panels (C9b, as TUIkitColorEditors with the gradient editor until 2026-10-12): they host ColorPickerPanel's body and chrome, and ColorPicker uses neither.

modules.name: TUIkitApp
modules.contents: App, Scene and its modifiers, and the POSIX console layer: the run loop, input, signals, the Terminal class, the isatty queries, renderOnce.

modules.name: TUIkitCommands
modules.contents: SwiftUI's commands (lane O13): Commands, CommandsBuilder, CommandMenu, CommandGroup, CommandGroupPlacement, EmptyCommands and the standard sets, TUIkit's DisplayCommands among them, the Scene modifiers that declare them, and the menu bar they draw. Above TUIkitApp because the modifiers extend Scene; on TUIkitPickers because DisplayCommands' submenus are Pickers; the run loop and the chrome host reach the bar through hooks that name nothing here.

modules.name: TUIkitScenes
modules.contents: The scenes shown over an app's windows (lane O9): Settings, presented as a sheet, and AlertScene, and the Scene modifiers for the alerts a scene presents. Above TUIkitApp because they are scenes, and on TUIkitPresentation, whose sheet and alert they are drawn with; the scene presenter reaches them through a hook (OverlayScene) that names nothing here.

modules.name: TUIkitFilePanels
modules.contents: The file panels (lane O10): fileImporter, fileExporter, fileMover and the fileDialog customizations, FileDialogBrowserOptions, the open and save panel TUIkit draws for them in a sheet, the folder listing behind it, FileDocument on Apple platforms and UTType where UniformTypeIdentifiers is absent.

modules.name: TUIkitTabImages
modules.contents: Tab's image: initialisers (the owner's TAB-IMAGE-NAME option 2, decisions C11): a tab whose picture is an image resource named by a string, found as Image(_:bundle:) finds it. A module of its own so that an app showing images pays nothing for tabs, and one using tabs nothing for the image decoders.

modules.name: TUIkit
modules.contents: The umbrella: Exports.swift's @_exported imports and nothing else.

declarations.why: R1: setLanguage and register(translations:) ask for a frame beside the views; without this pin the extension is seeded with LocalizationService in TUIkitStrings, which may not use TUIkitView (the lower check)
safeAreaInset is layout API (Base), not Lists

copyable, cuttable, pasteDestination and the clipboard commands are general API beside the clipboard they use (Base); the assigner lifts them to TextInput while it has the clipboard there, and they do not return
slimbase: the status bar state and the system items are what focus, controls and the input handler write; they and their public API stay in Base
S2: `.focusSection(_:)` is focus API (the base module): its modifier stays here, and A4 gave the method a block of its own in View+Events.swift

scheduled.why: both files get a Windows arm like their WASI one, with no pid_t in its signatures (A2)

accepted.why: R1: setLanguage(_:) and register(translations:) are declared in the base module, beside the views whose frame they ask for, on a TUIkitStrings type
R2: Image(_ source:), the bitmap path's initialiser, is declared in TUIkitBitmaps beside the pixels it makes; Image itself stays in the base module

TerminalClient's graphics-support API (graphicsSupported and its kin: A18's run-time detection) reads what TUIkitApp's startup handshake records, so the assigner lifts it into TUIkitApp. Every app imports TUIkitApp, so no app loses it. Plan section 4's review of lifted public API did not list it (found at 0c).
`.automatic` stays with List's other leading-dot styles: it is usable only through `.listStyle(_:)`, which is TUIkitLists'. DefaultListStyle itself comes down with the protocol (SP).
`.automatic` is usable only through `.navigationSplitViewStyle(_:)`, which is TUIkitNavigation's.
`.automatic` is usable only through `.pickerStyle(_:)`, which is TUIkitPickers'.
ForEach(_:editActions:content:) takes EditActions, which belong to List rows (TUIkitLists).
ForEach(sections:content:) rides on the section collection that the rules place in TUIkitLists (GroupSectionsOfContent).
init(wrappedValue:) where Value == TabViewCustomization: usable only with TabView's customization (TUIkitTabs).
init(wrappedValue:) where Value == TabViewCustomization: usable only with TabView's customization (TUIkitTabs).
init(wrappedValue:) where Value == TableColumnCustomization: usable only with Table's (TUIkitTables).
init(wrappedValue:) where Value == TableColumnCustomization: usable only with Table's (TUIkitTables).
slimbase: KeyNotation's question to the terminal client sits beside KeyNotation in Base, which re-exports TUIkitTerminalHost, so every importer of either sees it

O9 (decisions A26): dialogSeverity(_:), dialogIcon(_:) and dialogSuppressionToggle are Scene modifiers writing TUIkitPresentation's dialog environment, which TUIkitApp, which owns Scene, does not link; an app that uses them imports TUIkitScenes (the umbrella re-exports it).

O13: commands(content:), commandsRemoved() and commandsReplaced(content:) are Scene modifiers that declare commands and the menu bar they draw, which are TUIkitCommands'; an app that declares commands imports it (the umbrella re-exports it), and TUIkitApp, which owns Scene, must not see the commands.

MENUBAR: aboutPanel(…) states what the menu bar's About item shows, which is TUIkitCommands' (the About item, its alert and the Info.plist fallback live there), as commands(content:) declares the bar's commands; TUIkitApp, which owns Scene, has no menu bar to state it to.
slimbase: Image(_:bundle:) loads an asset-catalog bitmap; it is the bitmap path's API, beside Image(_:) from a file or URL, in TUIkitBitmaps

B-D3M-4: Image(_:scale:orientation:label:) and Image(decorative:scale:orientation:) draw a CGImage out through the bitmap path (_DecodedImage, PlatformImageLoader), beside Image(_:bundle:) and Image(_ source:), in TUIkitBitmaps; Image itself stays in the base module

TAB-IMAGE-NAME option 2 (decisions C11): Tab's image: initialisers find their image as Image(_:bundle:) does, the bitmap path's, so they are declared in a module of their own on TUIkitBitmaps and TUIkitTabs, which the umbrella re-exports: in TUIkitBitmaps every app showing an image paid for tabs (+10.9%), and in TUIkitTabs TUIkitImage would come under TUIkitColorPicker, whose panel is a TabView
TAB-IMAGE-NAME option 2 (decisions C11): the value-less image: forms, for the reason the value forms are declared there

TERMCAPS-API: the colour depth passes through to ColorDepth.current, which is TUIkitStyling's, and TUIkitTerminalHost, which owns TerminalCapabilities beside the other terminal facts, does not see TUIkitStyling; TUIkitFoundation sees both and re-exports both, so every importer of either sees it (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-24: one source of truth, no copy)

posix.why: POSIX-only APIs that do not compile on Windows. CLAUDE.md (relaxed by the owner 2026-10-07) lets them live in any module, isolated (own files, #if os(Windows) arms, a small protocol), never in a module that builds on Windows today: the four lower modules, which this map does not cover and CI's Windows lane guards. The plan still puts the console layer in TUIkitApp by design, so a use elsewhere is reported, as information. Types count too: plan section 4 (K6) says Windows signatures must not use pid_t.
posix.informational: POSIX outside TUIkitApp is allowed when isolated (CLAUDE.md, owner 2026-10-07): reported for information, not a new finding

witness_pairs.why: A type's conformance to the first protocol must see its conformance to each of the second: a constrained default (`extension P where Self: Q`) is chosen where T: P is checked, so a Q conformance in a module P's site cannot see is silently not used (M3's blank render). Pairs found in the sources' `extension P where Self: Q` are added to these.
